title: Putin and Kim Jong Un sign a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty in Pyongyang
body:
On 19 June 2024, Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a "comprehensive strategic partnership" treaty in Pyongyang. It was Putin's first visit to the North Korean capital since July 2000. The treaty includes a mutual defence clause, under which each side would assist the other if attacked. The full text was not released at the time of signing.

Putin said Russia did "not exclude" developing military-technical cooperation with North Korea, and tied this to Western deliveries of advanced weapons, including F-16 fighters, to Ukraine. Kim called the pact an alliance, described it as "strictly peace-loving and defensive", and expressed unconditional support for Russia's policies, including its war in Ukraine. Putin accused the United States, South Korea and Japan of raising tensions on the Korean Peninsula.

North Korea was founded in 1948 with Soviet backing and had a 1961 treaty with the Soviet Union that provided for mutual support in case of attack. Putin had hosted Kim at a September 2023 summit in Russia's Far East, which accelerated military cooperation. The U.S. State Department said deepening Russia-North Korea cooperation should concern anyone interested in peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula. The United States and its allies had accused Pyongyang of supplying ballistic missiles and artillery shells used in Ukraine, while Moscow and Pyongyang denied any weapons transfers.
